Definition: from G3844 and G5087; to place alongside, i.e. present (food, truth); by implication, to deposit (as a trust or for protection):--allege, commend, commit (the keeping of), put forth, set before.
BiblicalUsage: Paratithemi means to set before, to place alongside, to commit into keeping. Paul and Barnabas commend the elders to the Lord in Acts 14:23, and Paul commends the Ephesian elders to God and to the word of His grace in Acts 20:32. Timothy is told in 2 Timothy 2:2 to commit the things he has heard to faithful men, and in 1 Corinthians 10:27 the word is as plain as a meal: whatsoever is set before you, eat.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe commending is the act of faith that lets go: the elders are set before the Lord, the truth is set before faithful men, the meal is set before the guest. My position is that what I commit to God stays committed, and what I set before others should be worth eating.
